title: THz-Driven Floquet Spin Valve-Modulator
abstract: Within the scattering matrix ($S$-matrix) framework adapted to the high-frequency Floquet--Magnus formalism based on the length gauge, we investigate spin-dependent quantum transport in a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($π/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. We demonstrate the realization of a contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta--Das spin field-effect transistor with ferromagnetic leads operating at zero static magnetic field. It is shown that an off-resonance terahertz (THz) field enables high-precision switching between spin channels without altering the static parameters of the nanostructure. Driven by an electronic Vernier effect, the quantum interference in the asymmetric geometry yields a selective spin phase rotator alongside an ultra-high-contrast current-suppression regime (``optical shutter''). The proposed architecture is fundamentally robust against multiphoton leakage sidebands, offering a thermally immune, high-speed alternative to conventional semiconductor static spin transistors.
summary: The paper proposes using THz fields to control spin transport in an asymmetric quantum ring structure, mimicking the function of a spin transistor without physical gates. By leveraging Floquet theory and geometric phase effects, it achieves high-contrast switching and precise spin manipulation. This offers a robust, ultrafast alternative for spintronic devices.
main_problem: The research aims to create a high-speed, contactless electromagnetic analog of the Datta–Das spin field-effect transistor using time-varying THz fields.
main_result: The interplay between topological Aharonov-Casher phase and dynamic Floquet modulation enables both ultra-high-contrast current suppression (an 'optical shutter') and precise spin control in a 1D quantum ring.
method: The analysis employs the scattering matrix formalism adapted to the high-frequency Floquet–Magnus expansion, treating the system as an open quantum system coupled to reservoirs.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a 1D quantum ring with an asymmetric ($\pi/2$) configuration of quantum point contacts. The dynamics are governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian subjected to a linearly polarized THz electric field.
key_observables: Spin polarization $P(I)$, current suppression contrast, and the evolution of the relative spin phase difference $\Delta\varphi$.
important_parameters: THz frequency ($\omega$), Fermi energy ($E_F$), structural asymmetry ratio ($\pi/2$ configuration), and laser intensity ($I$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the high-frequency limit, utilizing the length gauge transformation to simplify the time dependence via the Floquet-Magnus expansion.
figures_summary: Figure 1 sketches THz field interaction paths in the ring arms; later sections discuss intensity-driven transport characteristics near exceptional points (EPs).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework using the $S$-matrix and Floquet theory to analyzing the effective Hamiltonian, and finally detailing how asymmetry and external driving fields induce spin control via interference effects.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from topological physics (Aharonov-Casher phase), periodically driven systems (Floquet engineering), and mesoscopic transport, offering a novel platform for ultrafast spintronics that avoids static material limitations.
